name: How do I estimate the square footage needed for a new kitchen layout?

mainEntity.name: How do I estimate the square footage needed for a new kitchen layout?
mainEntity.text: How do I estimate the square footage needed for a new kitchen layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: To estimate the square footage needed for a new kitchen layout, start with the main elements the room must hold: cabinets, sink, refrigerator, range or cooktop, prep space, trash storage, and any island or seating area. Then measure the clearances needed around those elements so people can move safely and doors can open fully. A layout that only works when walkways are narrowed or appliance clearances are ignored is usually not functional in real life. Homeowners should also factor in whether the kitchen will connect to dining, family room, or outdoor living areas. The goal is not just to fit everything in; it is to make the room comfortable and efficient. This is a useful unanswered question because many people know they want a bigger kitchen but do not know how much bigger. Strong content should explain how layout drives size, not the other way around.
acceptedAnswer.description: Estimate kitchen square footage by listing the appliances, cabinet runs, clearance zones, and any island or dining needs. Then check whether the proposed layout allows comfortable circulation and door swings. If the plan only fits on paper by shrinking walkways, the space is probably too small.
